clue.text: Introduction to Goethe, awfully flowery: a howler?

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter, so only the start of Goethe is taken
awfully suggests the letters of flowery are badly done, so they are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A critic sneers that Goethe's florid opening line is a real howler of a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges FLOWERY into REYWOLF, after the G from 'Introduction to Goethe'. 'howler' looks like a blunder, but here it is an animal that howls.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolves howl, so the grey species is literally a howler; the question mark flags the playful example.

clue.text: Trojan Queen and husband, each young at heart

indicators.note: at heart means placed in the middle of the other piece, so the young one goes inside

parts.note: a cub is a young animal

explanation.surface: A Trojan queen and her husband each feel young at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' puts CUB inside EA to give ECUBA, after H for husband.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Hecuba was Priam's wife and so queen of Troy.

clue.text: Leave relatives putting forward fashionable notion about work

parts.note: to park something is to leave it somewhere

indicators.note: putting forward means the fashionable bit is shifted to the front of the relatives phrase

parts.note: sons-in-law are relatives by marriage
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: Relatives on leave push forward a trendy theory about the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting forward' moves IN from SONS-IN-LAW to the front, giving INSONSLAW, after PARK.
explanation.definitionFit: The principle that work expands to fill the time available is a famous observation about work.

clue.text: One of cardinal virtue vis-à-vis the role of the sexes?

definitions.text: One of cardinal virtue vis-à-vis the role of the sexes?

parts.words: One of cardinal virtue vis-à-vis the role of the sexes?
parts.note: read one way it is the Victorian cardinal later made a saint; read another it is a modern man who shares domestic roles equally

explanation.surface: A churchman of great virtue is asked about attitudes to gender roles.
explanation.walkthrough: John Henry Newman was a cardinal canonised in 2019; a 'new man' is a man who rejects traditional sex roles.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the saintly Victorian cardinal and the egalitarian modern male go by this two-word name.

clue.text: A blow meeting teacher: turn!

parts.note: a head is a head teacher
to wind is to turn, as with a handle

explanation.surface: A punch lands on a teacher, who spins round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow' suggests a punch, but it is a wind that blows against you.
explanation.definitionFit: A headwind is a wind blowing straight against one's direction of travel, so a blow in the weather sense.

clue.text: Generally also filling in Times Jumbo

indicators.note: filling in means the word for also is stuffed into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as in four by three
jumbo means large
and means also

explanation.surface: Generally speaking, there is filler in the Times Jumbo crossword too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling in' puts AND between BY and LARGE. 'Times Jumbo' looks like the newspaper's big puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean on the whole or for the most part, an idiom for speaking in general terms.

clue.text: May, possibly, not name emperor?

indicators.note: not means the letter for name is left out of the month

parts.note: May is one example of a month

explanation.surface: Could May perhaps not name the emperor?
explanation.walkthrough: 'emperor' looks like a ruler, but the emperor is a large British species of the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor is a species of large moth, so the clue gives an example for the class.

clue.text: Figure, sort of square, placed behind houses

indicators.note: houses means holds inside, so the square goes within the other word

parts.note: to have placed one's behind down is to have sat
a T-square is a type of drawing square, so T

explanation.surface: A figure shaped like a square is positioned behind some houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' puts T inside SAT. 'placed behind' is a playful way of saying sat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stat is short for statistic, a numerical figure.

clue.text: Hockey player displaying energy: a key finisher

parts.note: go means energy or drive
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
an ender is one who ends, a finisher

explanation.surface: A hockey player shows energy as a key finisher of chances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key finisher' looks like a star scorer, but 'a key' is the Alt key.
explanation.definitionFit: In ice hockey the goaltender is the player who guards the net.

clue.text: Accommodation having café and places to stretch out

parts.note: a bar is a place serving food and drink, like a café
a rack was a torture frame for stretching victims

explanation.surface: Lodgings offer a café and places to relax at full length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretch out' suggests lounging; the racks are torture devices.
explanation.definitionFit: Barracks are buildings housing soldiers, a form of accommodation.

clue.text: Drive out in attempt to cross part of UK

indicators.note: to cross means the attempt spans the region, holding it inside

parts.note: to have a bash is to have an attempt
NI is Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A driving trip is an attempt to cross part of the UK.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cross' puts NI inside BASH.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish is to expel or force someone to leave, synonymous with driving them away.

clue.text: Turning letter in and out

parts.note: a letter here is something that lets people through, and this one rotates, admitting them in and out

explanation.surface: Someone keeps turning a letter over, putting it in and out of an envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' looks like correspondence but means one that lets, so an entrance that rotates.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating entrance lets people both enter and leave as it turns.

clue.text: City needing tips on sanitary distribution, eventually

indicators.note: tips on words are their two ends, so the first and last letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: A city eventually needs advice on how to distribute sanitary products.
explanation.definitionFit: Sydney is the largest city in Australia.

clue.text: Glider's manoeuvred by a female

indicators.note: manoeuvred means moved about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive spelt out as letters for the anagram

explanation.surface: A woman manoeuvres a glider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvred' rearranges GLIDERS plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: Griselda is a woman's name, famous from the patient wife of Chaucer's tale.

clue.text: Legally recover theatre tax

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre
a levy is a tax

explanation.surface: A legal case to claw back a tax on theatres.
explanation.definitionFit: To replevy is to recover seized goods by legal action, a law term.

clue.text: Impressive church ball eclipsing Mass this month

indicators.note: eclipsing means covering over, so the ball surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a yorker is a cricket delivery pitched at the batsman's feet
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics
inst is the old letter-writing abbreviation for this month

explanation.surface: A grand church ball overshadows the Mass held this month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eclipsing' puts M and INST inside YORKER. A yorker is a cricket ball bowled to land at the batsman's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: York Minster is the great Gothic cathedral of northern England.

clue.text: Stars in a certain type of film — nothing uplifting

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifting means read from bottom to top

parts.note: noir is a dark crime film genre
O is nothing, the figure zero

explanation.surface: Stars in a gloomy genre of film find nothing cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns NOIRO into ORION; the reversal covers both pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion is a prominent constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: Rashly fire entertaining school master on board

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the rearranged word holds the school
rashly means recklessly, suggesting the letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rash head teacher sacks the school master who gives on-board lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rashly' rearranges FIRE to FIER, and 'entertaining' puts SCH inside after FI. 'master on board' means a chess grandmaster, here Bobby Fischer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobby Fischer was a world chess champion, a master of the board game.

clue.text: Listener's shed remaining instruction to turn off

indicators.note: a listener hears the word for shed spoken

parts.note: a hangar is a large shed for aircraft
left means remaining, as in what is left

explanation.surface: A listener's shed is all that's left after an instruction to switch off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listener's' says HANGAR aloud, which sounds like 'hang a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver told to make a turn to the left off the road hears this idiom.

clue.text: Mustard dip

definitions.meaning: Colonel Mustard is a suspect in the board game Cluedo, giving the military rank's abbreviation
a dip between mountain peaks is a pass

explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Mustard is a suspect in Cluedo (Clue in the US), so 'Mustard' gives the rank's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for colonel and a mountain pass share these letters.

clue.text: Fastener initially buckled Ok won't come undone

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word that follows
come undone suggests a jumble of letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fastener first buckled, but okay, it won't come undone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come undone' rearranges OKWONT into OWKNOT after the B of 'buckled'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowknot is a knot tied with loops, used for fastening.

clue.text: Gain nothing when accepting old people's work

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the gain-nothing phrase holds the other letters

parts.note: to win is to gain
men are people
love is zero in tennis

explanation.surface: You gain nothing by taking on an old people's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when accepting' puts OMEN inside WIN, before LOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Women in Love is a novel by D H Lawrence, a literary work.

clue.text: Clearly see smoke rising over couple

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards

parts.note: a cig is a cigarette, a smoke
to ally is to join or couple

explanation.surface: Smoke can clearly be seen rising over a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns CIG into GIC between LO and ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Logically means in a clear, reasoned way, a near synonym for clearly.

clue.text: What bat in flight resembled for one: a rat, yet different

definitions.text: What bat in flight resembled for one

indicators.note: different means changed, so the letters are put into another order

explanation.surface: A bat in flight looks like a rat, yet it is different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges A RAT YET. In Alice in Wonderland, the Hatter sings that a bat flies 'like a tea-tray in the sky'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's parody compares a twinkling bat to a tray for tea in the sky.

clue.text: First rate accessory for hurling the Irish miss?

parts.note: A1 means first rate, read as letters AI
a sling is a device for hurling stones

explanation.surface: A top-notch accessory for the Irish game of hurling, perhaps?
explanation.walkthrough: Hurling is an Irish stick game, but here 'hurling' means throwing. A1 is written with I for the 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Aisling is a popular Irish girl's name, so one example of an Irish miss.

clue.text: Not quite result Liverpool player wanted, for certain

indicators.note: not quite means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to ensue is to result
Liverpool football club play in red and are known as the Reds

explanation.surface: A Liverpool player wanted a particular result, for certain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' cuts ENSUE to ENSU, then add RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ensured has been made certain or guaranteed.

clue.text: Claim one must have trousers on

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: bags is old slang for loose trousers
I is one as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Anyone claiming a pair must have trousers on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags I' is a British children's phrase for claiming something first, like 'dibs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Children say this phrase to stake a claim to something.

clue.text: Front of weathercock stopping at North

indicators.note: the compass points run N, E, S, W, so stopping at North cuts off the E for East

parts.note: a vane is a weathervane, such as a weathercock

explanation.surface: The front of a weathercock halts at the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping at North' drops the final E (East) so the word ends at N.
explanation.definitionFit: The van is the front of an army or procession, as in vanguard.
